doc.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011

title: Playing in Japan
summary: Japanese audiences are attentive; friends like Anthony Wonsey live in Tokyo.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Right. They download individual tunes or whatever. And you mentioned you had been to Japan to play? What’s that like?

It’s amazing. Yeah. That’s when you feel like sort of a rock star in the, I guess, jam band world. Over there they appreciate it so much differently than here. Like over here it’s appreciated but I don’t know how to explain it. Yeah, we’re like superstars over there as far as like the appreciation of the music. They understand what’s all going on, where in some cases over here people are just kind of listening. It’s always quiet. Like we played at the Blue Note in Tokyo and it’s sort of a jazz club setting, but during the song — dead silence by the crowd there. Like they were focused in and watching everything that goes on. And in the end, in the uproar, you know, a huge note, whatever, and then you have that kind of stuff and then they get down and they’re waiting. They’re just waiting for the next — and it’s intense.
It must have been a little disconcerting at first.

It was at first. But then you realize they’re really into it. They’re really into the music. And it’s definitely a different experience at first. I was like woah, another level of appreciation I guess.
Would you or any of the guys in your circle ever consider moving there?

I have. I have, yeah. I have friends that are over there that I went to Berklee with, and they have done that and they’re earning a good living too. Like for example my friend Anthony Wonsey is a jazz pianist. He played with Kenny Garrett and he still does the jazz circuit and does all the clubs and stuff. But he lives in Tokyo. And while he’s there he has a kind of like a hotel sort of situation, but he does that and he plays jazz gigs and he teaches there. And I have a few other friends. But not to mention just my friends who are Japanese. They were in Berklee and then moved back home.
